candidate_relations.reason: The MRI shows diffuse bilateral supratentorial white matter hyperintensity across all lobes, which is the hallmark of gliomatosis cerebri. PSP presents with midbrain/brainstem atrophy and hummingbird sign, not diffuse white matter infiltration.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: PSP is a tauopathy with midbrain atrophy and vertical gaze palsy; does not explain diffuse supratentorial white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensity

candidate_relations.reason: Corticobasal degeneration features asymmetric cortical and basal ganglia involvement, not the diffuse supratentorial white matter hyperintensity seen here consistent with gliomatosis cerebri.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: CBD is a tauopathy with asymmetric cortical atrophy; does not account for diffuse white matter T2 hyperintensity

candidate_relations.reason: Frontotemporal dementia is characterized by focal frontal and temporal atrophy/hypometabolism, not diffuse pan-lobar white matter hyperintensity as described in this case.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: FTD involves frontal/temporal lobar atrophy; does not explain diffuse white matter T2/FLAIR changes across all lobes

candidate_relations.reason: Multiple system atrophy presents with putaminal, cerebellar, or brainstem signal changes, not diffuse bilateral supratentorial white matter T2 hyperintensity spanning all cerebral lobes.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: MSA involves cerebellar/brainstem/striatal atrophy; does not produce diffuse supratentorial white matter infiltration

candidate_relations.reason: Metachromatic leukodystrophy can produce diffuse white matter T2 hyperintensity and progressive neurological decline, but it is a genetic lysosomal disorder (arylsulfatase A deficiency) presenting typically in childhood or young adulthood, not in a 78-year-old with no prior history. The reference diagnosis is gliomatosis cerebri, a neoplastic infiltrative process, which is a different diagnostic entity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: MLD is a lysosomal storage leukodystrophy causing white matter T2 hyperintensity but is a metabolic/genetic disease distinct from gliomatosis cerebri; onset at age 78 is atypical
